title: 영어브리핑_2026-11-13
korean_summary: 오늘 핵심(금): 이전가격 보고서 최종 확인·법인장 서명·컨설턴트 송부, 보낼 편지함 회신 재발송, 구매요청 2건 결재, 보험 회신 확인 후 본사 송부, 16시 금요일 정기 보고. 메일 조회 실패로 아침점검 기준.
paragraphs: Good morning, Anthony. Today is Friday, November thirteenth. This is your updated English briefing for today.
This version uses this morning's check. The mail system had an error this morning, so it is based on mail up to five o'clock yesterday afternoon. Some news may be missing. Please keep that in mind.
Today is the last working day of the week. Tomorrow is the health check day. So let's finish the important things before the team dinner tonight.

We have eight parts today. Part one is the top three for today. Part two is reports to collect. Part three is replies you owe. Part four is the schedule and deadlines. Part five is an English review. Part six is a short role-play. Part seven is a practice of key sentences. Part eight is the closing. Let's start.
Part one. The top three for today.
Number one. The transfer pricing report must be finalized today.

What is it? The local file is the transfer pricing report we must keep for the tax office. A consultant writes it for us. Yesterday morning, you told the chief accountant to go ahead with the final version. The chief accountant sent your answer to the consultant at ten nineteen. The consultant replied only ten minutes later, at ten thirty.

Why is it important? The deadline is today, November thirteenth. If the report is late, we may have a problem in a tax audit. Also, my director must sign it. If he is busy or out, it will be hard to finish on time.

Your first action today. Open the consultant's reply from yesterday at ten thirty. Check that it is really the final version, with no new questions. Then ask the chief accountant if the report book is ready. Bring it to my director for his signature in the morning. Make sure the chief accountant sends the signed copy to the consultant today.
Number two. A stuck email and two purchase requests.

What is it? This morning, your outbox still had one email that was not sent. It is your reply to the sample room manager about the dummies. Dummies are the dress forms in the sample room. Also, two new purchase requests are waiting for your approval in the groupware system.

Why is it important? The sample room manager may think you have not answered him. He may wash or move the dummies before your decision. For the purchase requests, many old requests are already late. We do not want new ones to wait too.

Your first action today. Open Outlook and check the outbox. If the reply is still there, send it again. Then open the groupware system and review the two purchase requests. Check the price, the reason, and the quote for each one.
Number three. The Friday reports and the insurance.

What is it? Every Friday, you send the weekly cash report to a head office manager at head office. You also send the weekly outsourcing report to my director. Both are set up to start at four o'clock. Also, about the insurance, my director replied to you at four twenty-seven yesterday. And the broker replied about the property insurance at three twenty-two.

Why is it important? Head office notices when the weekly reports are late. For the insurance, head office must report to the CEO one month before the policy ends. The head office manager is waiting for our answer.

Your first action today. Read my director's reply and the broker's reply first. If my director agreed, send the quote to the head office manager with a short summary. Then check the cash report and the outsourcing report drafts at four o'clock.
Part two. Reports to collect.

First, the purchasing staff. She owes you several things. The whiteboard quote was due on November seventh. The extra information for the sample room air conditioner was due yesterday. She also owes three October electricity VAT invoices. VAT means value added tax. And the first November period is not uploaded yet. Please ask her for a clear date for each item. Here is a sentence you can use.
"It has been almost a week since the deadline, and the whiteboard quote still has not come."

Second, the compliance officer. Head office sent a form about the fire extinguisher patch. The head office manager needs it by Monday, November seventeenth. Yesterday at five nineteen, you asked the compliance officer for the stock and the unit price. Please check her progress today, because tomorrow she is busy with the health check. Here is a sentence.
"Could you let me know where the stock and price list stands? I need it before Monday."

Third, The export staff. She is working on two things. One is a new clause in the trucking contract. It says who pays when cargo is damaged. The other is a notice to the trucking companies about the freight price change. Please ask her to show you both drafts before she sends them. Here is a sentence.
"Please make sure the contract says who pays for damaged cargo. Otherwise, we will have the same problem again."
Fourth, the IT staff. Two things are open with him. One is the new PC set purchase request. The other is the organization chart in the head office system. Here is a sentence.
"Could you let me know where the PC purchase request and the organization chart stand?"

Fifth, the items due tomorrow. All teams must upload customs and system data by Saturday. The quote for electrical checks and the CCTV quote are also due. And a leaving manager must return the residence card and the room key. Today is the last office day, so please remind them today. Here is a sentence.
"This is a friendly reminder. Please finish this by tomorrow at the latest."
Part three. Replies you owe.

First, the accountant. Yesterday, she sent two things. One is the October income statement. You need it for the monthly result report to my director. The other is her reply about her roles and responsibilities. Please review both. Your reply can start like this.
"Thank you for your prompt reply. I checked your roles list, and I have two questions."
Second, the accountant also found that one payment from head office has not come in yet. You need to ask head office. Your reply can start like this.
"Dear Sir, our accounting team has not received the payment yet. Could you please check the transfer status?"
Third, the payroll staff. She said the payroll for short-term workers will be done on November seventeenth. If the plan is fine, just give a short answer. Your reply can start like this.
"Thank you. Please go ahead on November seventeenth as planned."
Fourth, The head office manager. After you read my director's reply, send the insurance quote. Your reply can start like this.
"Dear Sir, as you suggested, we kept the same basis for machines as the current contract."
Part four. Schedule and deadlines.

Today, Friday. The transfer pricing report must be signed and sent. The weekly cash report goes to a head office manager. The outsourcing report goes to my director. At five thirty in the evening, there is a team dinner.

Tomorrow, Saturday, November fourteenth. It is the health check day for all workers. The customs and system data is due from all teams. The electrical check and CCTV quotes are due. A leaving manager returns the residence card and room key.
Sunday, November sixteenth. The GOH container will be loaded. GOH means garments on hanger.
Monday, November seventeenth. The fire extinguisher patch form is due to the head office manager. The short-term payroll is done. Head office also expects the October financial statements.
Part five. English review.
Let's review expressions from today's card, yesterday, three days ago, and last week.
The expression is "finalize." It means to make something final and complete. For example, "We need to finalize the transfer pricing file and sign it today." Now say it with me.
One more time. We need to finalize the transfer pricing file and sign it today.

The expression is "Unless I hear otherwise by ..., I will ..." It means, if nobody says no by that time, I will do it. For example, "Unless I hear otherwise by three p.m., I will sign the revised report." Now say it with me.
One more time. Unless I hear otherwise by three p.m., I will sign the revised report.

The expression is "It has been ... since ..., and ... still ..." It means, a long time has passed, but the thing is not done. For example, "It has been three weeks since we submitted the PR, and it still has not been approved." Now say it with me.
One more time. It has been three weeks since we submitted the PR, and it still has not been approved.
The expression is "expedite." It means to make something happen faster. For example, "Could you expedite the PR approval? The purchase has been waiting for weeks." Now say it with me.
One more time. Could you expedite the PR approval? The purchase has been waiting for weeks.
The expression is "comparable." It means under the same conditions, so we can compare. For example, "Please get comparable quotes for the same hard disk size." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please get comparable quotes for the same hard disk size.

The expression is "Could you let me know where something stands?" It means, please tell me how far it has gone. For example, "Could you let me know where the interlining upload stands?" Now say it with me.
One more time. Could you let me know where the interlining upload stands?

The expression is "Please make sure that ... Otherwise, ..." It means, check this carefully, or something bad will happen. For example, "Please make sure that the mainboard is the DDR4 version. Otherwise, the RAM will not fit." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please make sure that the mainboard is the DDR4 version. Otherwise, the RAM will not fit.
The expression is "overdue." It means the deadline has passed. For example, "Number one and number three are now overdue, so please finish them today." Now say it with me.
One more time. Number one and number three are now overdue, so please finish them today.
The expression is "scope." It means the range of work in a quote. For example, "Please ask all three companies to quote the same scope." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please ask all three companies to quote the same scope.
The expression is "prompt." It means fast, without delay. For example, "Thank you for your prompt reply. The lists are very useful." Now say it with me.
One more time. Thank you for your prompt reply. The lists are very useful.
The expression is "Please ... by ... at the latest." It means, this is the final time limit. For example, "Please send me the list by nine a.m. tomorrow at the latest." Now say it with me.
One more time. Please send me the list by nine a.m. tomorrow at the latest.
Part six. Role-play.
Here is a short talk. Anthony brings the transfer pricing report to my director for his signature. Listen carefully.
Anthony: Good morning, my director. Do you have five minutes? I need your signature on the transfer pricing report.
My director: Is that the consultant's report? The deadline is today, right?
Anthony: Yes, today. The consultant sent the final version yesterday. They incorporated our change in one section.
My director: What about the sister company? You asked them about it, didn't you?
Anthony: The consultant advised not to add a reason for the sister company. I agreed, because it may raise more questions in an audit.
My director: Okay. And the margin?
Anthony: It is within the range. As you said, we will watch the margin closely this year.
My director: Good. Where do I sign?
Anthony: Here, on the last page, please. the chief accountant will scan it and send it to the consultant this afternoon.
My director: Fine. Anything else today?
Anthony: Yes. About the insurance, I read your reply. Unless I hear otherwise by three p.m., I will send the quote to the head office manager today.
My director: That's fine. Go ahead.
Anthony: Thank you. I will also send the weekly cash report and the outsourcing report before the dinner.
My director: Good. See you at the dinner.
Part seven. Let's practice two key sentences from the role-play.
Sentence one. "We need to finalize the transfer pricing report and send it to the consultant today." Now say it with me.
One more time. We need to finalize the transfer pricing report and send it to the consultant today.
Sentence two. "Unless I hear otherwise by three p.m., I will send the quote to the head office manager." Now say it with me.
One more time. Unless I hear otherwise by three p.m., I will send the quote to the head office manager.
Now one bonus sentence, for the purchasing staff. "It has been a week since the deadline, and the quote still has not come." Now say it with me.
One more time. It has been a week since the deadline, and the quote still has not come.
Part eight. Closing.

Today has one main job. Get my director's signature on the transfer pricing report, and make sure it goes to the consultant today. After that, check the outbox for the reply to the sample room manager, approve the two purchase requests, and send the insurance quote to the head office manager. Before the dinner, send the weekly cash report and the outsourcing report.
It is Friday. Finish the urgent things in the morning, and enjoy the team dinner in the evening.
Have a good day, Anthony. See you on Monday.
